attributes.residual: RE-TYPED AGAIN, AND THE PRIOR RECORD'S 'lfs-vs-lfd TYPE DIFFERENCE' FRAMING IS WRONG. There is no f32/f64 type error and nothing semantics-adjacent about it. Baseline real 8, insns 111/111, opcode multiset IDENTICAL. The whole residual is that FOUR hoisted loads are dealt into four scheduler slots in a different ORDER, plus two FPR names. Target: +0x4c lfd f2,<pbLoad conversion magic>; +0x54 lfd f4,<viewport conversion magic>; +0x5c lfs f0,@lbl_80343EA0; +0x78 lfd f3,<1.0>. Ours: +0x4c lfd f4,<viewport magic>; +0x54 lfd f3,<1.0>; +0x5c lfd f2,<pbLoad magic>; +0x78 lfs f0,@lbl_80343EA0. So the target deals its three pool doubles in ASCENDING POOL ADDRESS order (which here coincides with first-use order) and puts the f32 global third; ours deals them in SOURCE STATEMENT order and defers the f32 global to last. NAMED MECHANISM: a four-way permutation of hoisted-constant load slots in one basic block, with an identical multiset and identical instruction count - SCHEDULE class, and a clean WebFrank candidate (pure permutation of independent loads with a trivially checkable dependence audit: all four define distinct FPRs and none is read before +0x88). AXES KILLED. (1) Statement reorder: moving `load = (f32)pbLoad;` above the two lbl_80344DDC/DE0 statements, so that source order would match target constant order, REGRESSED real 8 -> 40 and left the +0x5c/+0x78 swap rows completely unmoved - so the deal order is NOT a function of source statement order, which is the hypothesis this axis existed to test. (2) Local alias: hoisting the thrice-read `lbl_80343EA0` into a local f32 REGRESSED real 8 -> 43 and added an instruction (112 vs 111), with a named cause - the alias must stay live across the `bl floorf` call, so MWCC spills instead of reloading, and the reload-from-memory form is exactly what enables the target's `fnmsubs f31,f0,f1,f31` fusion at +0xc0. That fusion is load-bearing; do not reach for the alias axis on this function again.
